claim: For every finite oriented tree \(\vec T\), if \(P_{\vec T}\) is the reachability poset and \(a_2(P_{\vec T})\) is the maximum size of a subset containing no chain of three elements, then \(\operatorname{gp}(\vec T)=a_2(P_{\vec T})=\min_{\Pi}\sum_{C\in\Pi}\min\{2,|C|\}\), where \(\Pi\) ranges over all partitions of \(P_{\vec T}\) into chains.
integrity: The universal equality is proved mathematically; finite exhaustive computation is used only as a stress test. The supporting classical poset theorem is explicitly attributed, and no independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The formula is a reachability-poset min–max characterization rather than a degree-sequence closed form. Its tree-specific proof does not extend verbatim to DAGs with directed shortcuts, and an unindexed independent observation remains a literature risk.
title: Oriented-tree general position as a Greene–Kleitman two-family
